lines.en: Four feet tread the dry riverbed.
I walk along the dune.
My frill hangs low in the sun.
I stop and go, sweeping the ground.
The little one follows at my flank.
I scrape away a layer of dry sand.
I circle the territory.
The grass on this alluvial plain is sparse.
I push my way forward.
My tail sweeps behind me.
I have gone down into the wash again.
Today is the same patrol.
I cross a stretch of gravel.
I stand and chew slowly.
I stare at the horizon.
The wind blows sand against my legs.
I lower my head for two bites.
The little one is by my belly.
I lift a forefoot.
These dunes are mine.
I listen for a while.
I shake my neck.
The sun is beating down.

lines.zh: 我这颗头盾，低下来就是撞。
lines.en: My frill lowers, and that's a charge.
I keep the small one behind me.
There is not enough grass here.
I am waiting for the wind to drop.

lines.zh: 我的头盾挡住小崽，你退到沙外。
lines.en: My frill covers the calf; back away from the sand.
I lower my head right at you.
I am watching this side.
The little one is behind me.
What do you want.
Being stared at makes me restless.
I scrape twice with a foot.
The wind is blowing toward you.
Take one more step.
I let out a breath.

lines.zh: 四蹄在干沙上滑出两步。
lines.en: My four hooves slide two steps across the dry sand.
My frill is knocked askew.
I back off, shielding the young.
Not much pain, only anger.
I scrape the ground to steady myself.
Blood drips onto the sand.
I straighten my body again.

lines.zh: 头盾上留下一道白印，我记下了。
lines.en: A white mark on my frill — I won't forget it.
Not again.
What leaves are those.
I smell food.
Set it on the ground slowly.
I am guarding my young. Stand back.
There is not much of it.
I shifted one small step nearer.
Is this for me.
Just a little more.
I drive my frill in.
You are knocked back.
Sand kicks up between us.
I hold my ground.
I turn to shield the little one.
That was not a light hit.
I turn back to face you.
Your strength is no small thing.
I yielded half a step.
Again, and I will go at you.
We keep these dunes together.
The small ones walk between us.

lines.zh: 我低头碰了碰你的头饰。
lines.en: I lower my head against your frill.
The alluvial plain is wide enough.
We both smell it in this wind.
If strangers come, we both charge.
Walk slowly. Do not startle the young.
The sand is soft today.
One herd, one path.
Hold a while longer.
I dip my head to take it.
This mouthful is too small.
I cannot chew this.
I have a look at that stuff on the ground.
I nudge it toward the little one.
It grinds my teeth.
I will keep it and eat slowly.
There is no taste at all.
Who is that over there.
My whole body twists around.
The footsteps are close.
I lower my frill.
The little one backs away.
This is my ground.
Are you coming in.
I am ready to charge.

lines.zh: 我咬了一下空气，试试牙口。
lines.en: I bite the air once, testing my teeth.
I am counting your steps.
One more step.
My gaze is nailed to you.
The wind gave you away.
My eyes do not move off.
You circle; I turn with you.

lines.zh: 我侧过身，把冲沟口堵严。
lines.en: I turn sideways and seal the gully mouth.
You retreat, I stop.
I will not chase far.
The young are all behind me.
My feet are scraping the ground.
Try one step closer.
The dunes hide no one.
I do not call out. I brace.

lines.zh: 我把头盾压低，横在冲沟口。
lines.en: I lower my frill and block the gully mouth.
You are still hesitating.
I have left you a way out.
Come no nearer.
Nearly within reach.
I butt with my forehead.
My frill hits your chest.
I turn and charge again.
Dust covers the view.
I am guarding my young, so I do not follow.

lines.zh: 头盾顶在你胸口，你退我就停。
lines.en: My frill hits your chest; retreat, and I stop.
My front feet come down hard.
Again, and I charge again.
I am snorting for breath.
I hold my pace.
A new shadow on the dunes.
I climb out of the wash.
My frill shows first.
Footsteps sound on the dry riverbed.
A small herd slowly spreads.
The wind lifts the sand in sheets.

lines.zh: 牙道赫塔组的太阳，很晒。
lines.en: The Djadochta sun is harsh.
I lower my head to the ground.
The little one comes out from behind the slope.
I halt and look around.
The sand here is very dry.
I walk with deliberate steps.
I have found new ground.
I raise a forefoot.
There is no other scent in the wind.
I will keep this ground.
My shadow stretches out long.
I come to a slow halt.
The sand is burning, and I pull back.
My four feet jarred on landing.
Water covers my back and I panic.
The blast knocks me over.
Something is stuck in my flank.
This force goes into my bones.
Too little grass; I have grown thin.
Lightning struck and I leaped.
No sand here, and no ground.
